title: Sell Mineral Rights in Brookhurst, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Brookhurst, WY | Natrona County
metaDescription: Brookhurst sits on Casper's outskirts in Natrona County oil country. Get a straight, courthouse-checked read on your mineral interest before you sign anything.
heroLead: Brookhurst is close enough to Casper's edge that people here often assume their ground sits inside the old Salt Creek trend. Sometimes it does. I check before I say either way.
intro: Natrona County's century of oil development has left a patchwork of ownership around Casper, some tracts still generating royalty checks from mature production, others that were leased decades ago and never drilled. Brookhurst, sitting on the residential edge of the county, has examples of both, and the only way to know which applies to your family's interest is to pull the actual records.
If you've got a deed, a probate order, or even just a family name tied to this area, I'll start there and tell you what the county recorder actually shows.

sections.heading: Checking your specific position
paragraphs: I compare your legal description against the current Salt Creek unit boundary and any nearby producing spacing units on file with the Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission. That tells me whether we're discussing a producing royalty interest or undeveloped acreage.
Both categories have real value, they just get priced completely differently, and I'll explain which one your tract falls into before quoting anything.

sections.heading: Reconstructing ownership
paragraphs: A lot of Brookhurst-area mineral interests passed through Natrona County estates without much attention paid to them along the way. I can usually reconstruct a clean chain of title from the recorder's grantor-grantee index using whatever partial information you already have.

I've worked cases where an interest sat completely dormant in a family's name for two or three decades before anyone even remembered it existed. That doesn't affect its validity, the recorded ownership stands regardless of how much attention it's gotten.

faqs.question: Is Brookhurst part of an active oil field?
faqs.answer: Some nearby sections are, others aren't. I'll check your exact legal description before answering definitively.

faqs.question: I don't have the original deed. What do I do?
faqs.answer: Send me whatever you have, a tax bill, an old letter, a family name, and I'll search the county records myself.

faqs.question: How long does confirming ownership take?
faqs.answer: Usually a few days once I have enough to start the county records search.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure I even own anything here?
faqs.answer: That's a common starting point. Send whatever family information you have and I'll tell you plainly whether there's a recorded interest to work with.

faqs.question: Will you tell me if my interest isn't worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Yes. If the research shows there's genuinely little there, I'll say so directly rather than stringing you along.
